detail:
Across sources, the standard first-line medication approach for MCAS is combined H1 and H2 antihistamine therapy: a second-generation (non-sedating) H1 blocker plus an H2 blocker. ASCIA's 2025 position paper describes pharmacologic management as "trialled in a stepwise fashion under specialist guidance," naming cetirizine, desloratadine, and fexofenadine among H1 blockers and nizatidine and famotidine among H2 blockers. The MSD Manuals (Professional) states that H1 and H2 blockers "should be administered to all patients."

A positive clinical response to anti-mediator medication is also part of the diagnostic criteria for MCAS.

Medication decisions require a physician or specialist. Talk to your doctor before starting or changing any medication.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
